title: ETTAS: a modular aptamer-recruited platform for programmable translational activation.
data_url: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20849391 (raw western blot images); Europe PMC supplementary zip (Supplementary Materials.docx + Supplementary Table S5.xlsx)

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and unpacked the Europe PMC supplement: it contains only 'Supplementary Materials.docx' (9.5 MB, plasmid maps and sequences, text only) and 'Supplementary Table S5.xlsx'. I parsed S5 with openpyxl: one sheet, 96 data rows (149 rows of grid, the rest blank), 12 used columns (Aptamer_ID, Aptamer_Rename, Sequence, Total_Reads, P2, P4, P6, 'airosol', Nucleotides, P6/P2, P6/P4, P6/MIX), 96 unique 34-37 nt DNA sequences, read totals 43 to 88,456. I also queried the Zenodo record: it is a single 113 KB PDF of original western blot gels, CC-BY-4.0.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: That six rounds of SELEX (an iterative test-tube selection of binding DNA) were sequenced, that surface plasmon resonance and bio-layer interferometry affinity measurements were made on a few candidates, and that label-free mass-spectrometry proteomics was run. None of these raw or processed datasets is deposited anywhere I could find: no sequencing archive accession, no ProteomeXchange/PRIDE/iProX accession, and Europe PMC reports no database cross-references for this paper.

a1_downloadable.note: Supplement zip and the Zenodo gel-image PDF both download without login. But the only numeric table is Table S5; the SELEX sequencing pool and the proteomics quantification behind the paper's figures were never deposited.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Enrichment ratios (P6/P2, P6/P4) are already columns in Table S5, computed from the read-count columns in the same file.

a3_inputs_present.note: Full 34-37 nt DNA sequences are in column 3 of Table S5; no identifier lookups needed.

a4_units_stated.note: Columns are raw read counts (integers) and dimensionless ratios, which is unambiguous, but the 'airosol' column is undocumented and the 'P6/MIX' ratio divides by a 'MIX' column that is not in the file.

a5_enough_rows.note: KILLER. Table S5 holds 96 aptamer sequences. The checklist floor is ~1,500 labelled rows, or ~400 for classification. The underlying sequencing pool (millions of reads) that would have made this modellable was not deposited.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Methods say the library had a 40-nucleotide random region; the S5 header says 36 and the actual sequences are 34-37 nt. The paper never states how many sequences S5 contains, so there is nothing to check 96 against.

a8_label_provenance.note: Read counts come from real sequencing of selection rounds, so not another model's output; but the ratio labels are arithmetic on the feature-adjacent count columns, so only the ratio-versus-sequence task is meaningful.

existing_models.name: DeepAptamer (convolutional plus bidirectional long short-term memory network for aptamer affinity from SELEX sequencing)
existing_models.score_and_split: Abstract retrieved via search (Molecular Therapy Nucleic Acids 2024, PMC11787022): reported to beat prior models on SELEX data with experimental follow-up; exact metric and split not retrieved.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Identifying high-affinity sequences from early, unenriched SELEX rounds; not read in full.

existing_models.name: Restricted Boltzmann machine scoring of SELEX pools (generative, interpretable aptamer design)
existing_models.score_and_split: Abstract retrieved (PMC9553063): scores from one selection round correlate with experimental enrichment ratios at later rounds; numbers not retrieved.

existing_models.name: DL-SELEX / AptaVAE + AptaClux (variational autoencoders over SELEX next-generation sequencing pools)
existing_models.score_and_split: Abstract retrieved (PMC12713628, steroid-family aptamers); metrics and split not retrieved.

backbone.name: RNA-FM or a small k-mer/one-hot convolutional net (36 nt is far shorter than any nucleotide language model's useful context)

integration.partner_dataset: UTexas Aptamer Database / Apta-Index and published SELEX sequencing pools in the Sequence Read Archive
integration.join_key: none present; aptamer sequences would have to be matched as free strings, and these are novel 36-nt sequences against a different protein target
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Cannot be written: the 96 sequences were selected against dCas13a specifically and share no identifier with any public aptamer resource, so the join would be decoration.

controls.positive_control: Aptamer2, the one candidate the authors validated by surface plasmon resonance and bio-layer interferometry, should score high; but one positive example is not a control.
controls.negative_control: Label shuffling is computable on 96 rows but would be uninformative at that sample size.
controls.external_validation: None. The affinity measurements for candidate aptamers are shown only in figures, with no numeric table.

honest_claim_h3: At best: 'among the 96 most abundant sequences in one six-round SELEX experiment against one protein, sequence composition explains some of the round-6 enrichment ratio' - a statement about one selection run that no one could act on.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a short DNA sequence to predict how strongly it was enriched during test-tube selection against a Cas13a protein.
plain_idea.train_on: The 34-37 nucleotide DNA sequence of each selected aptamer, for the 96 sequences listed in Supplementary Table S5 (count verified by opening the file).
plain_idea.predict: The enrichment ratio between selection round 6 and round 2, which comes from high-throughput sequencing read counts of the DNA pool at each round.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Groups engineering CRISPR-Cas13 tools would like to pick strong protein-binding aptamers without running six rounds of selection; but with 96 sequences from one experiment, nothing learned here would transfer.

more_or_better_data.why: 96 summary rows against models such as DeepAptamer and the restricted Boltzmann machine work, which train on whole SELEX sequencing pools of millions of reads. Our table is a tiny top-abundance excerpt of one run.

confidence_score.why: No replicate selections and no per-sequence affinity measurements in the files, so there is no way to estimate measurement noise or calibrate a confidence.

models_beatable.why: The named models are 2022-2025 neural networks trained on far larger pools; 96 rows cannot support a competitive model, let alone an honest held-out evaluation.

guaranteed_improvement.why: No existing model targets dCas13a-binding aptamers, nothing joins on a shared key, and the evaluation split could not be matched - every condition fails.

ml_idea: The only modellable table is 96 SELEX-selected 36-nucleotide DNA aptamer sequences with round-by-round sequencing read counts and enrichment ratios; the task would be predicting enrichment from sequence. At 96 rows from a single selection run against a single protein, this is roughly 4x below the classification floor and 15x below the regression floor in the checklist. The paper's other quantitative assets - label-free mass-spectrometry proteomics and SELEX sequencing pools - were not deposited, and the only repository record is a 113 KB PDF of western blot gel images.

effort.compute_note: Estimated from the actual file: a 468 KB Excel sheet with 96 rows, parsed in under a second with openpyxl. Compute was never the constraint here.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the rows in Supplementary Table S5 - I did, and it is 96, which kills the project in one command.

verdict_reason: A5 fails hard: the only numeric data file holds 96 aptamer sequences, and the sequencing pool and proteomics behind the paper's figures were never deposited.
